title: The Broker of Stolen Songs
story: In the moor-market under rattling lanterns, Mirthquail has six stolen music boxes locked in a bramble cage, each tagged at 48 gold crowns. 'Buy all six and I'll knock off 25 percent,' she chirps, 'plus a flat cage-fee of 20 crowns, naturally.' Mr 6 empties his coin pouch onto the counting stone and starts figuring.
question: How many gold crowns must Mr 6 pay in total for all six music boxes?
solution: Six boxes at full price: 6 × 48 = 288 crowns.
praise: Finding the full price first was the right opening — one of the two adjustments (the discount or the fee) still needed its turn.
hint: Work the discount on the whole six-box price first; the cage-fee is added at the very end, not discounted.
victory: Mr 6 counts out exactly 236 crowns, not one more, and Mirthquail's bramble cage springs open — six music boxes play at once, and she flees from the harmony.
imagePrompt: A cloaked thistle-broker creature haggling across a lantern-lit moor market stall with a caped numeral 6 knight counting gold crowns, bramble cage of music boxes glowing behind her.
